title: Local regularization for multiclass learning
formal: Does every realizably PAC-learnable multiclass hypothesis class H admit a fixed local regularizer \(\psi :H\times X\to \mathbb{R} \ge 0\) such that every learner induced by \(\psi\), under the pointwise minimum-score rule below, PAC learns H? This is the existence part of the source question; optimal sample complexity is a separate refinement.
why: Tests whether a fixed preference over hypotheses at each prediction point is a general principle for multiclass learning. A negative answer would identify a limit of regularization even when improper prediction is allowed; a positive answer would give a common template for all learnable multiclass classes.
status_note: As of 11 September 2026, two checked preprints claim a negative resolution. Their theorem statements and local-regularization/PAC definitions match the main target, but the full impossibility proofs were not independently audited and no accepted publication was verified. Retained as uncertain rather than certified open or resolved.

sentences: A local regularizer fixes a score for every hypothesis and test point before seeing the training sample.
At prediction time it selects among the lowest-scored hypotheses consistent with the sample.
The question asks whether every realizably PAC-learnable multiclass class admits such a rule that succeeds under every tie-breaking choice.
Two preprints from July and August 2026 claim counterexamples under this definition.
Their statements match the main question, while independent verification of the claimed negative resolution remains outstanding.

upgraded_from.title: Can Local Regularization Learn All Multiclass Problems?

references.title: COLT / PMLR
references.authors: Julian Asilis; Siddartha Devic; Shaddin Dughmi; Vatsal Sharan; Shang-Hua Teng

definitions: Let X be an instance space, Y a label space that may be infinite, and \(H\subseteq Y^{X} a\) nonempty class of predictors \(h:X\to Y\). A distribution D on labeled examples \(X\times Y\) is realizable by H if some \(h*\in H\) satisfies PrD\([h*(x)\ne y]=0\). The risk of a predictor g is \(LD(g)\)=PrD\([g(x)\ne y]\). A learner A maps a finite labeled sample S to a predictor \(A(S)\), which need not belong to H. It PAC learns H if, for every \(\varepsilon ,\delta \in (0,1)\), there is \(mA(\varepsilon ,\delta )<\infty\) such that for every H-realizable D and every \(m\ge mA(\varepsilon ,\delta ), a\) sample S of m independent draws from D satisfies \(\Pr [LD(A(S))>\varepsilon ]\le \delta\). Probability spaces, predictors and learners are understood with measurable error events, so these probabilities are defined. There is no running-time requirement. For a nonempty realizable sample S, the version space \(H[S]\) consists of all \(h\in H\) agreeing with every labeled example in S. A local regularizer assigns each pair \((h,x) a\) nonnegative real score \(\psi (h,x)\), fixed before observing S. It is admissible only if a minimum score on \(H[S]\) is attained at every test point x and the induced prediction rules are well-defined; an empty argmin cannot make the claim vacuously true. A learner is induced by \(\psi\) when \(A(S)(x)\) belongs to {\(h(x): h\in\)argmin \(g\in H[S] \psi (g,x)\)} for every such S,x. On empty or unrealizable samples its behavior is unrestricted. The quantifier “every induced learner” includes every valid tie-breaking rule; its sample bound may depend on that learner. The regularizer can depend on H and x, but not on S, its size, its unlabeled points, \(D, \varepsilon\) or \(\delta\).
answer_criterion: Prove that every realizably PAC-learnable H has such an admissible regularizer, or give a PAC-learnable class H and prove that every admissible local regularizer induces at least one learner that is not PAC consistent in the stated distribution-independent sense. A favorable tie-breaking rule alone is insufficient. Neither a transductive separation nor failure of proper learning alone settles this PAC question.

context_blocks.title: A different preference at each test point
context_blocks.text: A regularizer expresses which hypotheses the learning rule prefers. Local regularization lets that preference depend on the new point being classified. After training, only hypotheses that fit the sample remain eligible, and the rule predicts using a least-scored eligible hypothesis at that point.

context_blocks.title: Why the prediction can be outside the class
context_blocks.text: One hypothesis might be preferred in one region of X and another in a different region. The resulting predictor can combine their labels without being a single hypothesis from H. This flexibility matters because some multiclass problems are learnable only by allowing such improper output.

context_blocks.title: Ties carry a real quantifier
context_blocks.text: The source asks the regularizer to succeed for every induced tie-breaking learner. If all scores are zero, the rule imposes no preference among sample-consistent hypotheses. Selecting one specially chosen successful learner from those ties would not show that the regularizer itself learns the class. Likewise, score minima must exist for the prediction rule to be meaningful.

context_blocks.title: Sample-dependent regularization is a different model
context_blocks.text: The source reports a general positive result when a local regularizer may first use the unlabeled training points. Here the score function is fixed independently of the sample. The question tests whether that extra sample information is necessary for a general multiclass learning rule.

context_blocks.title: Two 2026 claims of a negative resolution
context_blocks.text: Hou’s July preprint claims a countable learnable class beyond all local regularizers. The August preprint by Asilis and coauthors independently claims a PAC counterexample under the same worst-case tie convention and acknowledges Hou’s work. The checked statements match the main question, but their full lower-bound proofs have not been independently verified in this review. The card therefore records a claimed negative resolution with uncertain status.
